summary: Perf canary baseline refresh needed (tiered batching SLO gates) after legitimate improvements
description:
Request: Refresh perf-canary baselines for tiered batching SLO gates.

Context
- Since enabling workload signals + fast-tier admission control, perf canary is failing on 'regression' checks despite overall latency improving.
- Current baseline appears stale vs latest runtime behavior, causing noisy blocks on unrelated PRs.

Impact
- CI gating failures blocking runtime + scheduler PRs.
- Risk: teams may start bypassing perf checks / treating failures as expected.

What changed (suspected legit improvements)
- Scheduler wait-budget + admission control tuning for fast tier.
- Mixed-workload scenario updates in benchmark-lab.

Requested outcome
- Establish new baselines for affected scenarios (fast tier p99, standard tier p95 gates) and document sign-off.

Scope
- Top models and configs used in perf-canary today (see perf-canary config), with tier labels enabled.
- Regions/rigs: gpu-perf-ci runners only (not production).

Non-goals
- Do not change SLO targets or pass/fail thresholds in this ticket; only baseline refresh + approvals.

Owner
- Perf suite / scheduler: Marcus Reed
- CI reliability: Sahana Iyer

Approvals required before landing
- Runtime scheduling lead: Sofia Ivanova
- SRE (gating owner): Sean Gallagher
- Applied ML/Evals (sanity check on prompt sets): Claire Dubois (FYI only)

Proposed process (baseline refresh playbook)
1) Freeze inputs
   - Pin benchmark-lab revision and perf-canary revision for the baseline run.
   - Confirm prompt set version IDs used by tier scenarios.
2) Run baseline jobs
   - Run 10 iterations per scenario (fast tier p99, standard tier p95; include mixed streaming/non-streaming where applicable).
   - Collect variance stats and confirm no outliers from runner instability.
3) Generate candidate baseline update
   - Update baseline JSON/artifacts in perf-canary repo.
   - Include a diff summary: old vs new p50/p95/p99 + throughput.
4) Review + approvals
   - Sofia: confirm improvements align with expected scheduler change behavior (no hidden trade-off).
   - Sean: confirm thresholds remain meaningful and alerting/rollback expectations unchanged.
5) Merge + monitor
   - Merge baseline update.
   - Monitor 48 hours of perf-canary signal: failure rate, flakiness, and expected sensitivity.

Acceptance criteria
- Perf-canary passes for mainline/runtime PRs with no code changes (sanity).
- New baseline artifacts committed with documented run metadata (runner type, commit SHAs, timestamp).
- Approvals captured in comments from Sofia + Sean.
- Follow-up created if flakiness > 2% (CI instability) or if sensitivity becomes too low (fails to catch known-bad changes).

resolution: Baselines refreshed in perf-canary using pinned benchmark-lab/perf-canary revisions after legitimate latency improvements from tiered batching scheduler changes. Approvals obtained from Scheduling (Sofia Ivanova) and SRE gating owner (Sean Gallagher). Monitored 48h post-merge with no increased flakiness.
next_steps: If perf-canary sensitivity becomes too low (fails to catch known-bad scheduler changes), propose adding an additional mixed streaming scenario or tightening variance handling; otherwise no action.
